gh api repos/ashtom/entire-brain/pulls/55/comments/3515660504/replies -X POST -f body="We measured this scenario against the real schema before shipping the chunked version: the relations table has both \`idx_relations_from\` and \`idx_relations_to\` (semantic.go), and \`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN\` on the exact per-chunk query shows SQLite choosing a MULTI-INDEX OR plan (two indexed searches, no table scan) — measured ~27ms per 900-id chunk against a 500k-row table. Each chunk's work is proportional to its matching rows, which any implementation (temp-table join included) must also pay.

Binding the full global \`limit\` per chunk is required for merge correctness (each batch must return its own top-\`limit\` by id for the global top-N merge to be sound — the function comment explains this), and rows are deduped by rowid during the merge, so the buffer holds distinct matches, not chunks x limit.

The worst-case caller (viz's handleGraph) was also bounded in bed4fd80: \`relLimit\` is now ceilinged at 4x vizGraphMaxEdges (360k), so the many-chunks-x-huge-limit combination no longer occurs. Non-viz callers pass small symbol sets (single-node detail, replay subsets). A temp-table approach would also complicate connection handling (\`database/sql\` pools connections, so the TEMP table and query must be pinned to one \`sql.Conn\`) for no measured gain — keeping the simpler chunked merge." --jq '.id'
